cases.sentence: На ___, в 11 часов утра, Вронский выехал на станцию Петербургской железной дороги встречать мать, и первое лицо, попавшееся ему на ступеньках большой лестницы, был Облонский, ожидавший с этим же поездом сестру.
cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Next day at eleven o’clock in the morning Vronsky drove to the station of the Petersburg railway to meet his mother, and the first person he came across on the great flight of steps was Oblonsky, who was expecting his sister by the same train.

cases.sentence: – Но Алексея Александровича, моего ___, верно, знаешь.
cases.explain: «знаменитого зятя» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “But Alexey Alexandrovitch, my celebrated brother-in-law, you surely must know. All the world knows him.”

cases.sentence: – Да, он очень ___; немножко консерватор, но славный человек, – заметил Степан Аркадьич, – славный человек.
cases.explain: «замечательный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, he’s a very remarkable man; rather a conservative, but a splendid man,” observed Stepan Arkadyevitch, “a splendid man.”

cases.sentence: – Ну, и тем лучше для него, – сказал Вронский улыбаясь. – А, ты здесь, – обратился он к высокому ___ матери, стоявшему у двери, – войди сюда.
cases.explain: «старому лакею» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Oh, well, so much the better for him,” said Vronsky smiling. “Oh, you’ve come,” he said, addressing a tall old footman of his mother’s, standing at the door; “come here.”

cases.sentence: Слышался свист паровика на ___ и передвижение чего-то тяжелого.
cases.explain: «дальних рельсах» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The approach of the train was more and more evident by the preparatory bustle in the station, the rush of porters, the movement of policemen and attendants, and people meeting the train. Through the frosty vapor could be seen workmen in short sheepskins and soft felt boots crossing the rails of the curving line. The hiss of the boiler could be heard on the distant rails, and the rumble of something heavy.

cases.sentence: Он очень ___ и бывает неприятен, правда, но зато иногда он бывает очень мил.
cases.explain: «нервный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “No,” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, who felt a great inclination to tell Vronsky of Levin’s intentions in regard to Kitty. “No, you’ve not got a true impression of Levin. He’s a very nervous man, and is sometimes out of humor, it’s true, but then he is often very nice. He’s such a true, honest nature, and a heart of gold. But yesterday there were special reasons,” pursued Stepan Arkadyevitch, with a meaning smile, totally oblivious of the genuine sympathy he had felt the day before for his friend, and feeling the same sympathy now, only for Vronsky. “Yes, there were reasons why he could not help being either particularly happy or particularly unhappy.”

cases.sentence: – Графиня Вронская в этом отделении, – сказал ___, подходя к Вронскому.
cases.explain: «молодцеватый кондуктор» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Countess Vronskaya is in that compartment,” said the smart guard, going up to Vronsky.

cases.sentence: Слова кондуктора разбудили его и заставили вспомнить о матери и ___ с ней.
cases.explain: «предстоящем свидании» — the prepositional is used only after a preposition, for location or topic.
cases.translation: The guard’s words roused him, and forced him to think of his mother and his approaching meeting with her. He did not in his heart respect his mother, and without acknowledging it to himself, he did not love her, though in accordance with the ideas of the set in which he lived, and with his own education, he could not have conceived of any behavior to his mother not in the highest degree respectful and obedient, and the more externally obedient and respectful his behavior, the less in his heart he respected and loved her.
